title: Utilizing chemically induced dimerization of FKBP to analyze endocytosis by live-cell imaging in budding yeast
protocol: Revive yeast strain(s) from a glycerol stock by streaking out the strain on a YPD plate.
Incubate the plate upside down at 30°C for 2–3 days.
Inoculate a single colony into a culture tube containing 3 mL SC medium the day prior to imaging.
Incubate in culture tube rotator at 30°C for 12–16 hours.
Dilute the overnight starter culture to an OD600 of 0.1–0.2 in a total volume of 10 mL fresh SC medium.
Incubate the diluted culture in rotator at 30°C for 3–5 h, allowing cells to grow to early logarithmic phase (OD600 0.2–0.3).
Transfer 2.5 ml of early log phase cells to two new culture tubes labeled for drug or vehicle treatment.
Return the ethanol treatment tube to 30°C incubator.
Dissolve AP20187 in 100% ethanol to a concentration of 0.5 mM if purchased as a solid.
Store the 0.5 mM AP20187 solution at -20°C.
Add 25 μL of 0.5 mM AP20187 (resulting in a final concentration of 5 μM) to the treatment tube.
Incubate the culture containing AP20187 and ethanol vehicle control at 30°C for 90 minutes.
Remove the ethanol treatment tube from the incubator after 30 minutes of AP20187 treatment.
Add 25 μL of 100% ethanol to the removed treatment tube.
Incubate the added ethanol-containing tube at 30°C for an additional 90 minutes.
Transfer 1 mL of AP20187 treated cells to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 4,000 × g for 1 min.
Aspirate approximately 970 μL of supernatant, leaving behind about 30 μL and the yeast cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells by pipetting up and down.
Transfer 3 μL of the cell suspension to the center of a microscopy slide.
Cover the cell suspension with a glass coverslip.
Gently wipe the slide and coverslip with a kimwipe immediately before use to remove any debris.
Mount the prepared slide on a 100× oil immersion objective.
Use a spinning disk confocal microscope for imaging.
Focus on a medial focal plane at the cross-section of a group of cells using brightfield illumination.
Center approximately 10 budding cells in the field of view.
Capture time-lapse images at 1 s intervals for 90 s.
Set 488 nm laser line exposure to 250 ms.
Set 561 nm laser line exposure to 250 ms.
Use 50% laser power.
Optimize exposure and laser power prior to the experiment based on your imaging system and protein(s) of interest.
Match excitation wavelength to the fluorescent protein (FP) used, such as 488 nm for GFP and 561 nm for mCherry fusion proteins.
Adjust time-lapse duration and image interval according to the patch lifetime of the protein being studied.
Capture 2–3 additional time-lapse images using identical parameters.
Repeat steps 8–14 with the ethanol-treated cells 90 min following ethanol treatment.
Open a time-lapse image in SlideBook 6 and identify an actively budding mother cell to analyze.
Identify endocytic proteins as punctate structures along the cell membrane, persisting then disappearing over time.
Ensure that the cytosol region for fluorescence intensity measurement does not include area from the dimmer nucleus and vacuole.
Analyze mother cells only for differentiation and fluorescence intensity determination.
Create a mask within the time-lapse image (select Analyze > Create Mask).
Generate regions within the mask that cover the endocytic patch, cytosol of the mother cell, and background outside the cell.
Track the patch over time to record average fluorescence intensity values at peak intensity.
Subtract background fluorescence intensity from patch and cytosol intensities for correction.
Divide corrected patch intensity by corrected cytosol intensity to calculate the peak patch/cytosol ratio.
Visually identify the starting point of the patch in the time-lapse image.
Count the number of frames in which the protein is present at the patch.
Multiply the number of frames by the time-lapse image frame interval to determine the patch lifetime.
Repeat the analysis on 5 total cells in the time-lapse image.
Repeat the same analysis of 5 cells in a second time-lapse image, resulting in the analysis of 50 endocytic patches in total.
